goal: Lock the read-only production gap audit and the minimum supervised-production architecture contract without implementing runtime product behavior.
acceptance_conditions: The audit classifies current production capabilities into REUSE, ADAPT, MISSING, and DO NOT BUILD from live canonical repository evidence.
The contract preserves canonical Blueprint v3.13 authority and does not reintroduce stale v3.0 facts such as unverified STEM/CIP status.
The contract freezes the existing truth engine against hypothetical semantic churn and requires real consequential production failures before mutation.
The contract keeps external discovery, Gmail, Google Sheets, Google Drive, Vercel, Claude, and other providers as replaceable adapters around the owned truth core.
The first implementation seam is limited to Gmail alert ingestion -> normalization -> exact-role dedupe -> JOBS Sheet persistence + LOG records.

No runtime code, schema, test, Golden set, Candidate Truth, Employer Truth, Match Truth, package behavior, submission behavior, Vercel deployment, or external provider integration is implemented by this milestone.
PURSUE and SUBMIT remain distinct human-controlled boundaries; system recommendation never constitutes human pursuit authorization.
The branch ends as a doctrine-only candidate requiring independent architecture review and Bora acceptance before any Slice 1 implementation authorization.
After Bora acceptance and merge, a separate bounded governance-sync milestone must refresh canonical continuity/checkpoint pointers before Slice 1 implementation may be authorized.
Doctrine acceptance never authorizes Slice 1 implementation; Slice 1 requires the post-merge continuity sync plus a separate allowed-paths mutation contract and Bora explicit authorization.

Slice 1 consumes the canonical untrusted `DiscoveryLead` boundary concept and exact employer/system + requisition/opportunity identity rule; it does not invent a parallel lead model or fuzzy exact-role identity.
stop_conditions: Stop if completing this contract requires any runtime/product implementation or any path outside allowed_paths.
Stop if the contract would weaken canonical truth/provenance, Golden tests, Assurance, human submission control, or provider replaceability.
Stop if a provider-specific convenience is being promoted into canonical truth architecture rather than retained as an adapter.
Stop at doctrine acceptance/rejection; Slice 1 implementation requires a separate bounded mutation contract.
